ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state/reaction structure, ignoring the curved arrows. The lower fragment is a six-membered cyclic ketone structure; there is a carbonyl C=O on the ring, and it is connected to an oxygen-containing enol/oxide anion part, with an exocyclic C=C and C–O visible. The upper fragment is a structure containing nitrogen and a sulfone group, recognizable as N≡N–N–S(=O)2–Me, and is marked with charges. Reasoning: Count by fragments and do not count hydrogen-related bonds. The lower fragment includes 6 intraring C–C bonds, 1 carbonyl C=O bond, 1 alkene C=C bond connected to the oxygen-containing carbon, and 1 C–O bond, totaling 6 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 9 bonds. The upper fragment includes 1 N≡N bond, 1 N–N bond, 1 N–S bond, 2 S=O bonds, and 1 S–Me bond, totaling 6 bonds. The total is 9 + 6 = 15.

method.method_draft: Count bonds by fragment. In the lower fragment: count 6 ring C–C bonds, 1 carbonyl C=O bond, 1 alkene C=C bond to the oxygen-bearing carbon, and 1 C–O bond, giving 9. In the upper fragment: count N≡N, N–N, N–S, two S=O bonds, and S–Me, giving 6. Add all components: 9 + 6 = 15.

method.method_draft: Assign heavy-atom degrees from the visible connectivity. Lower fragment: carbonyl ring carbon degree 3, substituted ring alkene carbon degree 3, four remaining ring carbons degree 2 each, carbonyl O degree 1, exocyclic carbon degree 2, terminal O degree 1; degree sum = 18, so 18/2 = 9 bonds. Upper fragment: terminal N degree 1, central diazo N degree 2, N attached to S degree 2, S degree 4, two O atoms degree 1 each, Me carbon degree 1; degree sum = 12, so 12/2 = 6 bonds. Total = 9 + 6 = 15.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: A bond connection is an edge between two heavy atoms; each edge contributes 1 to the degree of each endpoint, so total bonds equal half the total heavy-atom degree sum. Implicit H atoms are ignored, and Me is treated as a carbon node bonded to S.
